mechanism_narrative: Sustained quarterly growth in GDPC1 (demand) predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as expanding demand signals economic strength and investor optimism.
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during periods of sustained GDPC1 growth or during contraction phases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in FEDFUNDS above 2% triggers negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as higher interest rates signal tightening monetary policy, compressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day returns not negative when FEDFUNDS crosses above 2%, or if the rate increase is temporary rather than sustained.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS is very low (e.g., <1%) and UNRATE rises above 6.5%, the interaction signals accommodative monetary policy offsetting tight labor market pressures, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns negative despite the FEDFUNDS <1% and UNRATE >6.5% combination, or if the condition occurs without positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in FEDFUNDS below 2% amplifies positive 60-day S&P 500 returns as stronger monetary easing signals increased investor confidence.
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS <2% in late-cycle expansion periods, or if the regime isn't late-cycle.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDPC1 (demand) and INDPRO (supply) above their 5-year averages triggers negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as inflationary pressures emerge from overproduction and excessive demand.
failure_condition: 20-day returns positive despite both GDPC1 >12000 and INDPRO >105, or if the thresholds aren't met but returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6% triggers negative 5-day S&P 500 returns as tight labor markets signal higher inflation expectations, reducing equity valuations.
failure_condition: 5-day returns not negative when UNRATE crosses above 6%, or if the increase is temporary.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained monthly growth in INDPRO (supply) predicts positive 60-day S&P 500 returns as increased production signals economic strength and investor optimism about future profits.
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly positive during sustained INDPRO growth or during contraction phases.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary easing cycle (FEDFUNDS <1%), high HOUST (housing demand) signals robust demand, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as both factors boost market confidence.
failure_condition: 20-day returns negative despite FEDFUNDS <1% and HOUST >600 combination, or if the trigger occurs without positive returns.
